mainTopic: אנינות and eating קדשים: the night after burial, and the story of אהרן's sons and the burned חטאת
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: the night after burial is still treated as אנינות, because חכמים strengthened their own rules even more than Torah rules. Then a ברייתא explains three phrases משה used on the day אהרן's sons died. One of them teaches that כהנים in אנינות must eat the קדשים. A second ברייתא seems to say the opposite: the חטאת was burned because of אנינות, and that was correct. שמואל answers that the two ברייתות follow two different תנאים. רבי נחמיה says the חטאת was burned because of אנינות, while רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say it was burned because of טומאה. רבא answers differently: both ברייתות follow רבי נחמיה, because one speaks of one-time קרבנות and the other of קרבנות for all generations. The גמרא then retells the conversation between משה and אהרן twice, once by each view. In both readings משה rules out each possible problem, and אהרן proves with a קל וחומר from מעשר that an אונן may not eat קדשים. The amud ends as משה begins to accept אהרן's answer, and the פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Sages strengthened their own rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier point. The night after burial gets the strict rule of אנינות because חכמים reinforced their own rules more than Torah rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages gave their own rules extra strength, even more than Torah rules have.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the discussion from before. It explains why the night after the burial day is still treated as אנינות, even though the אנינות of that day is only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you would expect a rabbinic rule to be lighter than a Torah rule. Here the גמרא says the opposite: חכמים sometimes made their rules stricter, so that people would take them seriously. That is why the rabbinic אנינות also covers the night that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The status of a mourner right after a close relative dies, which limits eating קדשים

steps.whatToRemember: A rabbinic rule can sometimes be applied more strictly than a Torah rule. The reason is to make sure people respect it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying rabbinic law is more important than Torah law. It means only that חכמים sometimes made their rules stricter so they would be kept.

phrases.english: And the Sages made a reinforcement for their words
more than those of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים עָשׂוּ חִיזּוּק לְדִבְרֵיהֶם יוֹתֵר מִשֶּׁל תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion that began earlier in the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The night after burial has אנינות even though that day's אנינות is מדרבנן, because חכמים reinforced their rules.

steps.title: Three phrases of command spoken by משה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains three phrases משה used on the day of נדב and אביהוא's death. One of them teaches that כהנים in אנינות must eat the קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'For so I am commanded,' 'as I commanded,' and 'as ה׳ commanded.' 'For so I am commanded' teaches that they must eat it even in acute mourning. 'As I commanded' is what he told them at the time of the incident. 'As ה׳ commanded' means: I am not saying this on my own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. The ברייתא gives a meaning for each of three different 'command' phrases in ויקרא פרק י.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main point is in the first phrase. משה told אהרן and his sons to eat the קדשים even though they were אוננים. The other two phrases add that משה said this when it happened, and that it came straight from ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of the incident
Not on my own, not from myself

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the idea that a כהן in אנינות may be required to eat קדשים. The next step challenges this idea.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"For so I am commanded," "as I commanded," "as the Lord commanded";
"For so I am commanded": they shall eat it in acute mourning,
phrases.notes: "It" means the קדשים that אהרן and his sons were given to eat that day.

phrases.english: "As I commanded": he said it to them at the time of the incident,
phrases.notes: The incident is when they burned the חטאת instead of eating it.

phrases.aramaic: ״כַּאֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳״ – לֹא מֵאֵלַיי אֲנִי אוֹמֵר.
phrases.english: "As the Lord commanded": I do not say it on my own.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, connected by the theme of אנינות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אונן כהן must eat קדשים. This is learned from כִּי כֵן צֻוֵּיתִי.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the burning was correct
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says the חטאת was burned because of אנינות, and the פסוק כָּאֵלֶּה supports this. That seems to contradict the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: it was burned because of acute mourning. That is why it says, 'such things as these.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that seems to clash with the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said אוננים must eat the קדשים. The second says burning the חטאת because of אנינות was right, since אהרן's argument 'such things as these happened to me' was accepted. So which is it: may an אונן eat, or not?

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction from another source
Such things as these, אהרן's words in ויקרא 10:19

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
it was burned because of acute mourning,
phrases.notes: "It" is the חטאת that אהרן and his sons burned that day.

phrases.english: that is why it says: "such things as these"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:19.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that אוננים must eat קדשים (step 2).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא says the burning was justified by אנינות. That suggests an אונן may not eat.

steps.title: Two ברייתות, two opinions
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says there is no real contradiction. One ברייתא follows רבי יהודה and the other follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי יהודה, and that one follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the contradiction. He says the two ברייתות simply follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not try to make both sources agree. Instead he says each ברייתא follows a different תנא who disagree about this story. The first ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and the second follows רבי נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction is solved by an argument between תנאים, רבי יהודה against רבי נחמיה, about how to read the story of the burned חטאת.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: It is not difficult;

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הָא רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה.
phrases.english: this is Rabbi Yehuda, that is Rabbi Neḥemya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources between two תנאים (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות follow one view, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ברייתא follows רבי יהודה and the second follows רבי נחמיה.

steps.title: The ברייתא that shows the dispute between רבי נחמיה and רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי נחמיה says the חטאת was burned because of אנינות, while רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say it was burned because of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: They burned it because of mourning, and that is why it says 'like these.' This is the view of רבי נחמיה. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say: It was burned because of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves שמואל's answer by quoting a ברייתא where רבי נחמיה and רבי יהודה really do argue about why the חטאת was burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the two ברייתות follow two different תנאים. This ברייתא shows that this argument exists: for רבי נחמיה the reason was אנינות, but for רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון it was טומאה. So the ברייתא that requires an אונן to eat follows רבי יהודה, and the one that says they burned it because of אנינות follows רבי נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: The state of a close mourner on the day of the death, before burial
They burned it, meaning the חטאת

phrases.english: As it is taught:
They burned it because of acute mourning,
phrases.notes: "It" is the חטאת that משה asked about.

phrases.english: that is why it says: "Like these."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:19

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Nechemya.
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon say:
It was burned because of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for שמואל's claim that רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה argue.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's answer that the two ברייתות follow two different תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the argument between רבי נחמיה and רבי יהודה with רבי שמעון

steps.title: Three proofs that the חטאת was not burned because of mourning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון give three reasons why the burning could not have been because of אנינות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was burned because of mourning, then all three חטאת offerings should have been burned. Another point: they could have eaten them at night. Another point: wasn't פינחס with them?
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the same ברייתא, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון back up their view with three arguments against the אנינות explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, three חטאת offerings were brought that day, yet only one was burned, so mourning could not be the reason. Second, mourning only blocks eating during the day, so they could have waited and eaten at night. Third, פינחס was there and was not in mourning, so he could have eaten it.

keyTerms.meaning: All three of them, meaning the three חטאת offerings of that day
Son of אלעזר, a כהן who was not in mourning

phrases.english: For if you say
that it was burned because of acute mourning,
then all three of them should have been burned.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean the same here.

phrases.english: Another point:
they would have been fit to eat them in the evening.
phrases.notes: Mourning only stops eating during the day, so waiting until night would have solved the problem.

phrases.english: Another point:
Wasn't פינחס with them!
phrases.notes: He was not a mourner, so he could have eaten it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאִם אַתָּה אוֹמֵר מִפְּנֵי אֲנִינוּת נִשְׂרְפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, giving רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון's reasons for their view.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the חטאת was burned because of טומאה, not אנינות
steps.raayaSupportSource: Three logical points: three חטאות but only one was burned, eating at night was possible, and פינחס was not in mourning

steps.title: רבא: both ברייתות can follow רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both ברייתות follow רבי נחמיה. One talks about one-time קרבנות and the other about קרבנות for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Both follow רבי נחמיה, and there is no contradiction. Here it speaks about one-time offerings, and there about offerings for all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer from שמואל: no need to split the ברייתות between two תנאים, because they speak about different kinds of קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For one-time קרבנות of the inauguration, משה told the mourning כהנים to eat. For permanent קרבנות that would be brought in every generation, like this חטאת, the כהנים were right to burn it because of אנינות. So רבי נחמיה can agree with both ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one; both
One-time קרבנות, brought only for that special occasion
קרבנות brought in all future generations
And it is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about the facts of the story. He is only showing a second way to make the two ברייתות fit together, without needing רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: רבא said:
Both this and that follow Rabbi Nechemya,
and it is not difficult;
here it speaks of one-time offerings,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא where the mourning כהנים had to eat.

phrases.english: there it speaks of offerings for all generations.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא where they burned the חטאת because of mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the contradiction from step 3, different from שמואל's answer in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ברייתא speaks about a different type of קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות must follow two different תנאים, as שמואל said.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבי נחמיה: mourners eat one-time קרבנות but do not eat permanent ones.

steps.title: How does each side explain the פסוקים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי נחמיה and the רבנן each read the conversation between משה and אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does רבי נחמיה explain these פסוקים, and how do the רבנן explain these פסוקים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next part: it wants to see how each side reads the פסוקים of the story in a way that fits its view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים in ויקרא 10:16-20 describe משה questioning אהרן about the burned חטאת. Each side needs to explain this exchange: רבי נחמיה with אנינות as the reason, the רבנן with טומאה as the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: How does he explain or make sense of
The Sages; here רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה הֵיכִי מְתָרֵיץ לְהָנֵי קְרָאֵי,
phrases.english: How does Rabbi Nechemya explain these verses,
phrases.notes: The verses are ויקרא 10:16-20, the exchange between משה and אהרן.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן הֵיכִי מְתָרְצִי לְהוּ לְהָנֵי קְרָאֵי?
phrases.english: and how do the Rabbis explain these verses?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה הֵיכִי מְתָרֵיץ לְהָנֵי קְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting out the argument, the גמרא turns to how each side reads the פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How each opinion explains משה's questions and אהרן's answers in the פסוקים

steps.title: רבי נחמיה's reading: משה checks for other problems first
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי נחמיה, משה first asked whether the blood went inside or the meat left its area, and אהרן said no to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה explains it like this: 'Why did you not eat?' משה said to אהרן: Maybe its blood went into the inner sanctuary? He answered: 'Its blood was not brought in.' Maybe it went outside its boundary? He answered: It stayed in the holy area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering for רבי נחמיה by showing how he reads משה's questions to אהרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי נחמיה's reading, משה is checking for other reasons that would require burning: blood brought inside, or the meat leaving its allowed area. אהרן rules out both, so the only remaining reason is אנינות, which fits רבי נחמיה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside its boundary, the area where it must stay

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya explains them like this:
"Why did you not eat":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:17

phrases.english: משה said to אהרן:
Perhaps its blood entered the innermost sanctum?
phrases.notes: If that happened, the חטאת would have to be burned anyway.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: ״הֵן לֹא הוּבָא אֶת דָּמָהּ״.
phrases.english: He said to him: "Behold, its blood was not brought in."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:18

phrases.english: Perhaps it went outside its boundary?
He said to him: It was in the holy area.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה מְתָרֵיץ לְהוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question from step 8 with רבי נחמיה's reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה ruled out blood brought inside and the meat leaving its area, and אהרן confirmed neither happened, leaving אנינות as the reason.

steps.title: משה suggests the offering was ruined by mourning
steps.stepSummary: משה suggests that the חטאת was disqualified because it was offered in אנינות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה said: Maybe you offered it while you were in אנינות, and that made it invalid?
steps.whatsHappening: משה, according to רבי נחמיה's reading, raises a new possible reason why the חטאת was burned: maybe it was offered by mourners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, אהרן said that neither the blood nor the meat went to the wrong place. So משה looks for another problem. A regular כהן who is an אונן may not do the עבודה, so if אהרן's sons offered it, the קרבן would be פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The status of a close relative of someone who died, on the day of the death

phrases.english: But perhaps you offered it while in mourning
phrases.notes: משה is talking about אהרן's sons, whose brothers נדב and אביהוא had just died that day.

phrases.english: and so disqualified it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא בַּאֲנִינוּת אַקְרֵיבְתּוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אהרן ruled out the blood and meat problems, משה raises a new possible problem.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ordinary כהנים who were אוננים did the עבודה, the קרבן would be disqualified, and maybe that is why it was burned.

steps.title: אהרן answers that he offered it himself
steps.stepSummary: אהרן answers that he, the כהן גדול, offered it, not his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: אהרן said: משה, did they offer it? I offered it!
steps.whatsHappening: אהרן rejects משה's suggestion. He points out that he himself did the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול is allowed to serve even while he is an אונן. So the offering was not made invalid by אנינות. This leaves אנינות as a problem only for eating the חטאת, which becomes the topic next.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest, who may serve even as an אונן

phrases.english: He (Aharon) said to him: Moshe,
was it they who offered it?!
I offered it!
phrases.notes: As the כהן גדול, אהרן was allowed to serve even as a mourner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מֹשֶׁה, וְכִי הֵם הִקְרִיבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers משה's suggestion from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual correction: the person who offered it was allowed to serve as an אונן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The offering was done by אוננים who may not serve, so it was invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: אהרן, the כהן גדול, offered it, so the offering itself was valid.

steps.title: משה argues it should have been eaten
steps.stepSummary: משה argues that since nothing went wrong, they should have eaten the חטאת even in אנינות, as he had commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה said: The blood was not brought inside, and the meat stayed in the holy area. So you should have eaten it as I commanded, meaning you should have eaten it even in אנינות.
steps.whatsHappening: משה now challenges אהרן: if the קרבן was completely valid, why didn't you eat it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every reason to burn the חטאת has been ruled out. משה points to his own command that day to eat the קרבנות even while mourning. So in his view, burning it was a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: Behold, its blood was not brought (inside)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: ״הֵן לֹא הוּבָא אֶת דָּמָהּ״
phrases.english: And he (Moshe) said to him: "Behold, its blood was not brought (inside)"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:18

phrases.english: and it (the meat) was in the holy area,
so "you should certainly have eaten it, as I commanded",
meaning: they should eat it even in mourning.
phrases.notes: משה had told them that day to eat the מנחה even though they were mourners.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר לוֹ: הֵן לֹא הוּבָא אֶת דָּמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With every reason for disqualification ruled out, משה argues the חטאת should have been eaten.
steps.kashyaTarget: אהרן's decision to burn the חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה commanded them to eat in אנינות, and the קרבן was valid, so it should have been eaten.

steps.title: אהרן says the command was only for one-time offerings
steps.stepSummary: אהרן answers that משה's command to eat in אנינות applied only to קדשי שעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אהרן said: "Such things have happened to me. If I had eaten the חטאת today, would it be good in ה׳'s eyes?" Perhaps you heard the permission only about one-time offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: אהרן defends burning the חטאת. He says the permission to eat while mourning covered only that day's one-time קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches רבא's distinction in step 7 between קדשי שעה and קדשי דורות. The חטאת that was burned was a permanent kind of קרבן, so the special one-day permission did not include it.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings brought only once, for that occasion
Would it be good in ה׳'s eyes?
Such things have happened to me

phrases.english: He (Aharon) said to him: "Such things have happened to me,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:19. אהרן is speaking about the death of his two sons.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָכַלְתִּי חַטָּאת הַיּוֹם, הַיִּיטַב בְּעֵינֵי ה׳״ –
phrases.english: and if I had eaten the sin offering today, would it be good in ה׳'s eyes?"

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא לֹא שָׁמַעְתָּ אֶלָּא בְּקׇדְשֵׁי שָׁעָה?
phrases.english: Perhaps you heard it only about one-time offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא לֹא שָׁמַעְתָּ אֶלָּא בְּקׇדְשֵׁי שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers משה's challenge from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the command
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The command to eat in אנינות covers all קרבנות.
steps.terutzMaskana: It covers only קדשי שעה, not the permanent חטאת.

steps.title: Proof from מעשר שני that a mourner may not eat permanent offerings
steps.stepSummary: אהרן proves with a קל וחומר from מעשר that an אונן may not eat קדשי דורות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the permission applied to permanent offerings, that could not be right because of a קל וחומר from מעשר, which is less strict. The Torah says about מעשר, "I did not eat from it in my mourning." So surely an אונן may not eat permanent קרבנות!
steps.whatsHappening: אהרן backs up his answer with a proof. He shows why the permission could not apply to permanent קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני is less holy than קרבנות, yet an אונן may not eat it. So a more holy thing, permanent קרבנות, must certainly be forbidden to an אונן. That means the special permission must have been only for that day's one-time offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings that apply for all generations
Reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter one
Here, מעשר שני, the second tithe
In my mourning (from the word אונן)

phrases.english: For if it were about offerings for all generations,
there is a קל וחומר from the lighter case of מעשר:
if about מעשר, which is lighter, the Torah said:
"I did not eat from it in my mourning";
phrases.notes: דברים 26:14

phrases.english: then for offerings for all generations, all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי בְּקׇדְשֵׁי דוֹרוֹת, קַל וְחוֹמֶר מִמַּעֲשֵׂר הַקַּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אהרן's claim from step 13.
steps.raayaObject: An אונן may not eat קדשי דורות, so the permission was only for קדשי שעה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from מעשר, based on the פסוק לֹא אָכַלְתִּי בְאֹנִי מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that an אונן may not eat regular קרבנות. It explains why the permanent חטאת could not be eaten that day.

steps.title: משה agrees and admits he forgot
steps.stepSummary: משה immediately accepts אהרן's argument and openly admits he had heard the הלכה but forgot it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away, "משה heard, and it was good in his eyes." He agreed, and he was not embarrassed. He did not say "I never heard this." Instead he said, "I heard it and I forgot."
steps.whatsHappening: The conversation ends. משה admits that אהרן was right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "וישמע" (he heard) is read as showing that משה had heard this הלכה before. So משה did not cover up his mistake by claiming he never learned it. He honestly admitted that he had forgotten it.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי נחמיה, the חטאת was burned because of אנינות. אהרן offered it validly as כהן גדול. But a mourner may not eat permanent קרבנות, and the permission to eat in mourning was only for that day's one-time offerings. משה agreed and admitted that he had forgotten.

phrases.english: Immediately, "Moshe heard, and it was good in his eyes"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:20

phrases.english: he admitted, and Moshe was not embarrassed
to say "I did not hear it,"
rather he said: "I heard it, and I forgot."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד וַיִּשְׁמַע מֹשֶׁה וַיִּיטַב בְּעֵינָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: משה accepts אהרן's proof from step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: משה accepts that an אונן may not eat קדשי דורות. That is why the חטאת was burned, and משה honestly admits he forgot this הלכה.

steps.title: How do רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון explain the verses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון read the משה–אהרן conversation in the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון explain these verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just explained the conversation one way. Now it asks how רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, who see the story differently, would read the same verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold that the חטאת was burned because it became טמא, not because of אנינות. So the earlier reading of the verses does not fit them, and the גמרא needs a new reading that matches their view.

keyTerms.meaning: How do they explain (fit together) them?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon
phrases.notes: These are the תנאים who say the חטאת was burned because it became impure.

phrases.english: how do they reconcile them (the verses)?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הֵיכִי מְתָרְצִי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רבי נחמיה's reading, the גמרא returns to the second half of its question from step 8: how do רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון read the same פסוקים?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the verses of the משה–אהרן conversation fit the view that the חטאת was burned because of טומאה.

steps.title: משה's first question: did the blood go inside?
steps.stepSummary: According to their reading, משה's question 'why didn't you eat it' meant: maybe the blood was brought into the inner sanctuary, which would require burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: They explain it like this: 'Why didn't you eat the חטאת in the holy place?' means: maybe its blood was brought into the innermost area?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by retelling the conversation. משה's first question is understood as checking whether the blood was brought inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood of an outer חטאת is brought inside, the meat must be burned and not eaten. So משה is checking whether that is why they burned it.

keyTerms.meaning: The innermost area, deep inside the משכן

phrases.english: They reconcile them like this:
"Why have you not eaten the sin offering
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:17

phrases.english: in the place of the Sanctuary?" –
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets. With it, the quote matches the פסוק's full wording.

phrases.english: Perhaps its blood entered the innermost sanctum?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי מְתָרְצִי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 16 by retelling the conversation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The conversation is read as משה checking possible reasons the חטאת had to be burned, starting with blood brought inside.

steps.title: אהרן: the blood was not brought inside
steps.stepSummary: אהרן answers with the פסוק: the blood was not brought into the inner sanctuary.
steps.simpleTranslation: אהרן said to him: 'Look, its blood was not brought into the holy place inside.'
steps.whatsHappening: אהרן rules out משה's first worry. The blood stayed outside where it belonged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is how this reading explains the פסוק 'הן לא הובא את דמה'. It is אהרן's answer to the blood question.

phrases.english: He said to him:
"Behold, its blood was not brought
into the Sanctuary within."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:18

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: הֵן לֹא הוּבָא אֶת דָּמָהּ אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ פְּנִימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers משה's question from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual denial backed by the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the blood went inside, which would require burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blood was not brought inside, so that was not the reason.

steps.title: משה's second question: did the meat leave the courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: משה asks whether the חטאת went outside its allowed area and became disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it went outside its boundary?
steps.whatsHappening: משה checks a second possible reason for burning: maybe the meat left the area where it may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת may only be eaten inside the courtyard. If it goes out, it becomes פסול and must be burned.

phrases.english: Perhaps it went outside its partition?
phrases.notes: The boundary here is the courtyard of the משכן, where the חטאת must stay.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא חוּץ לִמְחִיצָתָהּ יָצָאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the blood question is ruled out, משה raises the next possibility.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it left the courtyard, it became פסול, which would explain the burning but also mean something went wrong.

steps.title: אהרן: it stayed in the holy area
steps.stepSummary: אהרן answers that the חטאת stayed inside the holy area the whole time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Look, it was in the holy area.
steps.whatsHappening: אהרן rules out the second worry. The meat never left the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both the blood problem and the leaving-the-area problem are ruled out. משה will keep checking other possible reasons.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Behold, it was in the sacred area.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: הֵן בַּקּוֹדֶשׁ הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the meat left the courtyard.
steps.terutzMaskana: It stayed in the holy area.

steps.title: משה's third question: did אנינות disqualify it?
steps.stepSummary: משה asks whether the offering was brought by mourners in אנינות and became פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe you offered it while in אנינות and made it פסול?
steps.whatsHappening: משה raises a third possibility: the כהנים were אוננים, and that may have disqualified the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular כהן who is an אונן may not do the עבודה. If he does, the offering becomes פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The state of a close mourner on the day of death

phrases.english: But perhaps you sacrificed it in acute mourning
and disqualified it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא בַּאֲנִינוּת אַקְרֵיבְתּוּהָ וּפְסַלְתּוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next possibility after step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אונן doing the עבודה makes the offering פסול.

steps.title: אהרן: I offered it, not my sons
steps.stepSummary: אהרן answers that he, the כהן גדול, did the offering, and a כהן גדול may serve in אנינות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: משה, did they offer it, so that אנינות would make it פסול through them? I offered it!
steps.whatsHappening: אהרן rules out the third worry. His sons did not offer it; he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול may do the עבודה even as an אונן, so his אנינות does not disqualify it. This repeats the same answer we saw in step 11, now inside this new reading.

phrases.english: He said to him: Moses,
was it they who sacrificed it –
phrases.notes: 'They' means אהרן's sons.

phrases.english: that acute mourning would disqualify it through them?!
I sacrificed it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מֹשֶׁה, הֵן הִקְרִיבוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies who actually did the עבודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sons, as אוננים, offered it and made it פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן גדול offered it, and his אנינות does not disqualify.

steps.title: משה's fourth question: did it become טמא through carelessness?
steps.stepSummary: משה asks whether, in their grief, they were careless and the חטאת became טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe, because of your bitter grief, you were careless with it and it became טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: משה raises a new possibility that was not in the earlier reading: the meat became טמא because they were not careful while grieving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question fits רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, who hold the חטאת was burned because it became טמא. משה is asking whether that טומאה came from carelessness.

phrases.english: Or perhaps, due to your bitterness,
you were negligent with it and it became impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא אַגַּב מְרָרַיְיכוּ פְּשַׁעְתּוּ בַּהּ וְאִיטַּמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next possibility after step 22, and the one that is unique to this reading.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it became טמא through carelessness, אהרן would be at fault for losing the offering.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question is the main difference from the earlier reading. It matches the view that טומאה was the real reason for the burning.

steps.title: אהרן: I would never treat holy offerings with contempt
steps.stepSummary: אהרן strongly rejects the idea that he was careless with holy offerings, even in his tragedy.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: משה, is that how you see me, that I would disrespect holy offerings? 'Such things have happened to me.' Even if these and more like them happened, I would not disrespect holy offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: אהרן rejects the fourth worry. He was not careless, no matter how great his grief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהרן reads the פסוק 'ותקראנה אתי כאלה' as: even if these tragedies and more like them came upon me, I would still guard holy offerings. So if it became טמא, it was not from carelessness.

phrases.english: He said to him: Moses,
am I like this in your eyes,
that I would treat offerings consecrated to Heaven with contempt?!
"There have befallen me such things as these";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:19

phrases.english: even these and more like these –
I would not treat offerings consecrated to Heaven with contempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מֹשֶׁה, כָּךְ אֲנִי בְּעֵינֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denial of carelessness, supported by reading the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In his grief, אהרן was careless and the offering became טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: אהרן would never be careless with holy offerings, no matter what tragedy came upon him.

steps.title: משה: then you should have eaten it even in אנינות
steps.stepSummary: משה argues that since nothing went wrong, they should have eaten the חטאת even in אנינות, as he had commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If 'its blood was not brought inside' and it stayed in the holy area, then 'you should surely have eaten it in the holy place, as I commanded', meaning they should have eaten it even in אנינות!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that every problem has been ruled out, משה challenges אהרן: why didn't you eat it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה takes אהרן's own answers (blood not inside, meat stayed in the holy area) and argues that the offering was fine to eat. Since משה had commanded them to eat even in אנינות, burning it seems wrong. This sets up אהרן's coming answer.

phrases.english: He said to him: And if
"Behold, its blood was not brought,"
and it was in the sacred area –
"You should certainly have eaten it in the sacred area,
as I commanded,"
they should eat it in acute mourning!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וְאִי הֵן לֹא הוּבָא אֶת דָּמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on all of אהרן's answers to make a direct challenge, like step 12 in the earlier reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to burn the חטאת instead of eating it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no disqualification happened, the command to eat even in אנינות should have been followed.
steps.whatToRemember: In רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון's reading, משה rules out four problems (blood inside, leaving the area, אנינות, careless טומאה), then challenges אהרן for not eating it in אנינות.

steps.title: אהרן answers that the command applied only at night, proven by a קל וחומר from מעשר
steps.stepSummary: אהרן answers משה's challenge. משה's command to eat holy food in אנינות must have been meant for the night, because during the day a קל וחומר from מעשר forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אהרן said to משה: Maybe what you heard was only about the night. If it were about the day, there is a קל וחומר from מעשר, which is less holy. The Torah says about מעשר: 'I have not eaten of it in my mourning.' So holy offerings, which are more holy, must be forbidden all the more.
steps.whatsHappening: אהרן defends why they did not eat the חטאת. He says משה's command to eat while in mourning could only have been about the night after the death, not the day itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה had argued that nothing went wrong, so they should have eaten as he commanded. אהרן limits that command to the night. His proof is a קל וחומר: the Torah forbids an אונן to eat מעשר, which is less holy, so קדשים, which are more holy, must be forbidden during the day.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument: if a rule applies to the lighter case, it surely applies to the stricter case
Tithe. Here it means the second tithe, which is eaten in ירושלים and is less holy than offerings
Strict holiness. Here it means the meat of offerings
In my mourning, while I was an אונן
At night, here the night after the day of death

steps.whyThisMatters: This קל וחומר is the source that an אונן may not eat קדשים, learned from the פסוק about מעשר.

phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps you did not hear
phrases.notes: This is אהרן speaking to משה.

phrases.english: except regarding the night;
for if it were during the day,
there is a קל וחומר from tithe, which is lenient:
Just as regarding tithe, which is lenient, the Torah said:
"I have not eaten of it in my mourning";
phrases.notes: דברים 26:14

phrases.english: sacred food, which is stringent, all the more so, is it not?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: שֶׁמָּא לֹא שָׁמַעְתָּ אֶלָּא בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers משה's argument from Step 25 that they should have eaten the חטאת in אנינות
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of משה's command (night only) and supports the limit with a קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה's command to eat in אנינות applied even during the day of death
steps.terutzMaskana: The command applied only at night. During the day an אונן may not eat קדשים, by קל וחומר from מעשר

steps.title: משה immediately accepts אהרן's argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the פסוק that shows משה immediately accepted what אהרן said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately: "And משה heard..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts the פסוק showing that משה accepted אהרן's answer right away. The rest of the פסוק continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיד stresses that משה did not argue further. The פסוק "וישמע משה" closes the exchange: אהרן's reasoning was correct, and not eating the חטאת was proper.

keyTerms.meaning: And משה heard. He accepted the argument

phrases.english: Immediately: "And Moses heard,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:20. The rest of the פסוק comes next: it was good in his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד וַיִּשְׁמַע מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that משה accepted אהרן's answer from Step 26
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: משה conceded to אהרן: an אונן does not eat קדשים during the day of death
